newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to seek second round of budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: Israel to seek second round of budget cuts.

text.p: The Israeli government, facing a yawning budget deficit this year, said on Wednesday it would seek a second round of budget cuts for 1997 before parliament votes on the first round sent it in October.

"We're at a very difficult crossroads," Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said after revealing that his government would be asking for two billion shekels in spending cuts on top of the 4.9 billion in the original 1997 spending package of 190.8 billion shekels.
"We received a difficult legacy from the previous government, but how difficult became apparent only in recent days," said Netanyahu, who ousted the Labour party from government in May elections.

Netanyahu and Finance Minister Dan Meridor did not say where the additional cuts would come from but vowed they would not raise taxes as an alternative. "We will do everything not to increase the tax burden. We already have one of the highest tax burdens in the world," said Netanyahu.
A senior government official said the additional cuts would not affect the defence budget.
Treasury sources said they were considering reducing the ministries' procurement budgets and trimming social welfare spending.

Netanyahu said detailed spending cuts would be worked out after November 30, when the latest 1996 revenue figures are in, and a proposal will be given to parliament in early December for approval by the end of the month.
The government already faces tough opposition in parliament to the original cuts on the ground they will hurt lower-income groups hardest.

But this year's budget is running well in excess of the deficit target as government revenues have fallen behind projections. As a result, Israel's current account deficit is expected to widen to $5 billion this year from $4.1 billion in 1995.
"We have a very dangerous deficit in the balance of payments, which will grow worse in the next one-to-two years if we don't cut," Meridor warned.
